# CloudEvents Specification Required Attribute Set

The CloudEvents core specification defines a minimal set of exactly **four required context attributes** that MUST be present in every compliant CloudEvent: **`id`**, **`source`**, **`specversion`**, and **`type`** [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). Normatively, these four attributes are specified in the **CloudEvents Core Specification, Version 1.0.2** (`cloudevents/spec.md`, under **Context Attributes → REQUIRED Attributes**, canonical anchor `https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/v1.0.2/cloudevents/spec.md#required-attributes`) [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md) and enforced structurally in the official JSON Schema (`cloudevents/formats/cloudevents.json`) via `"required": ["id", "source", "specversion", "type"]` [spec/cloudevents/formats/cloudevents.json at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/formats/cloudevents.json). Release `v1.0.2` (tagged `ce@v1.0.2` and aliased at `ce@stable`, released February 5, 2022) is the latest stable release listed in the official CNCF Graduated CloudEvents repository, with specification-tracking commentary confirming it remained stable at `1.0.2` as of September 2026 [CloudEvents Specification - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec).

Every other component of a CloudEvent envelope—including the four core optional context attributes (`datacontenttype`, `dataschema`, `subject`, and `time`), any extension context attributes, and even the domain-specific event payload (`data`, or `data_base64` in the JSON Event Format)—is `OPTIONAL` at the core specification level [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). As the CloudEvents Primer (`cloudevents/primer.md`) explains, the specification authors deliberately limited the required set to attributes considered vital to all events across all use cases, keeping the common envelope small while accommodating specialized metadata through optional and extension attributes [spec/cloudevents/primer.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/primer.md).

## Normative Specification of the Four Required Attributes

Requirement keywords (`REQUIRED`, `MUST`, `MUST NOT`, `SHOULD`, `SHOULD NOT`, `RECOMMENDED`, `MAY`, `OPTIONAL`) throughout the CloudEvents specifications follow **RFC 2119** [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). The table below summarizes the exact normative definitions, abstract types, constraints, and examples from `cloudevents/spec.md` (**Context Attributes → REQUIRED Attributes**) [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md).

| Attribute | Abstract Type & Encoding | Mandatory Constraints (`REQUIRED` / `MUST`) | Non-Mandatory Guidance (`SHOULD` / `RECOMMENDED` / `MAY`) | Official Specification Examples |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **`id`** | `String` (allowable Unicode sequence) [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md) | `REQUIRED`; `MUST` be a non-empty string; `MUST` be unique within the scope of the producer; producers `MUST` ensure `source` + `id` is unique for each distinct event [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). | Re-sent duplicate events (e.g., due to a network error) `MAY` carry the same `id`; consumers `MAY` assume events with identical `source` and `id` are duplicates [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). | An event counter maintained by the producer; a UUID [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). |
| **`source`** | `URI-reference` (RFC 3986 §4.1) [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md) | `REQUIRED`; `MUST` be a non-empty `URI-reference`; producers `MUST` ensure `source` + `id` is unique for each distinct event, collaborating if multiple producers share one `source` [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). | An absolute URI is `RECOMMENDED`; applications `MAY` assign a unique `source` per producer using UUIDs, URNs, DNS authorities, or an application-specific scheme [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). | `https://github.com/cloudevents`; `mailto:cncf-wg-serverless@lists.cncf.io`; `urn:uuid:6e8bc430-9c3a-11d9-9669-0800200c9a66`; `/cloudevents/spec/pull/123`; `/sensors/tn-1234567/alerts`; `1-555-123-4567` [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). |
| **`specversion`** | `String` (allowable Unicode sequence) [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md) | `REQUIRED`; `MUST` be a non-empty string; compliant producers targeting the v1.0.x line `MUST` use the value `"1.0"`; all events in the same batch `MUST` share the same `specversion` [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). | For release-candidate releases, a suffix might be used for testing purposes [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). | `"1.0"` [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). |
| **`type`** | `String` (allowable Unicode sequence) [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md) | `REQUIRED`; `MUST` be a non-empty string [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). | `SHOULD` be prefixed with a reverse-DNS name indicating the organization that defines the event type's semantics; format is producer-defined and might include type versioning [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). | `com.github.pull_request.opened`; `com.example.object.deleted.v2` [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). |

### Composite Uniqueness and Deduplication

A common implementation misconception is that `id` alone must be globally unique. The core specification deliberately avoids requiring globally unique IDs so that producers can rely on lightweight local mechanisms such as monotonically increasing counters [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). Instead, uniqueness is normatively defined over the **composite pair `source` + `id`** [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). If a single `source` covers more than one producer, `cloudevents/spec.md` states that those producers `MUST` collaborate to guarantee `source` + `id` uniqueness; alternatively, an application `MAY` assign a distinct `source` to each producer so local IDs never collide [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md).

This composite identity directly supports idempotent event handling: when a duplicate event is retransmitted after a transport failure, the producer `MAY` reuse the original `id`, and consumers `MAY` treat events with identical `source` and `id` values as duplicates [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). The CloudEvents Primer (`cloudevents/primer.md`) further advises against overloading `id` with domain semantics, noting that any external meaning encoded in the string is irrelevant to CloudEvents and should not be relied upon beyond uniqueness checking [spec/cloudevents/primer.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/primer.md).

### URI-Reference Flexibility vs. Absolute URIs for Source

In its **Type System** section, `cloudevents/spec.md` distinguishes between `URI` (an absolute URI per **RFC 3986 Section 4.3**) and `URI-reference` (a URI reference per **RFC 3986 Section 4.1**) [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). Because `source` is typed as `URI-reference`, both absolute URIs and relative or application-specific references—such as `/cloudevents/spec/pull/123`, `/sensors/tn-1234567/alerts`, or `1-555-123-4567`—are legally valid [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). However, the specification explicitly notes that an **absolute URI is `RECOMMENDED`** (for example, an internet-wide DNS-anchored URI or a UUID URN) so that event sources remain unambiguous when routed across shared buses or external organizational boundaries [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md).

### Specversion Pinning and Batch Uniformity

Even though the CloudEvents 1.0 specification has received two patch releases—`v1.0.1` in December 2020 and `v1.0.2` on February 5, 2022 [CloudEvents |](https://cloudevents.io/)—`cloudevents/spec.md` requires compliant producers to emit **`"1.0"`**, including only the major and minor version numbers [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). This design allows clarifying patch revisions without altering wire serialization [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). Under `docs/GOVERNANCE.md`, breaking changes increment the major version while keeping the minor version at zero, ensuring `specversion` always takes the form `X.0` [spec/docs/GOVERNANCE.md at main - cloudevents - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/docs/GOVERNANCE.md).

`specversion` also enforces the **only cross-event constraint** on CloudEvents batches in `cloudevents/spec.md`: individual events inside a batch may differ in `source`, producer, `type`, or content type, but all CloudEvents within the same batch `MUST` carry the same `specversion` value [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md).

### Event Type Semantics and Routing

The `type` attribute identifies the kind of occurrence and is commonly used by intermediaries and consumers for routing, observability, and policy enforcement [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). While its internal structure is producer-defined, `cloudevents/spec.md` advises that it `SHOULD` begin with a reverse-DNS prefix indicating the organization responsible for the event type's semantics [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). As `cloudevents/primer.md` clarifies, CloudEvents prescribes no single versioning convention; producers may embed a version indicator directly in `type` (for instance, `com.example.object.deleted.v2` or an unstable-version marker), rely on separate schema references, or omit versioning entirely [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md).

## Cross-Cutting Core Constraints and Scope Boundaries

Beyond per-attribute rules, the four required attributes inherit three normative constraints from the surrounding sections of `cloudevents/spec.md`. First, under the **Type System**, any `String`-typed attribute (`id`, `specversion`, and `type`) is restricted to allowable Unicode characters: control characters in `U+0000`–`U+001F` and `U+007F`–`U+009F` (inclusive, which guards against header-breaking characters like `U+000A` newlines), Unicode noncharacters, and unpaired UTF-16 surrogates (`U+D800`–`U+DBFF` and `U+DC00`–`U+DFFF` unless properly paired) are explicitly disallowed [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). Second, under **Naming Conventions**, all attribute names—including the four required names—`MUST` consist solely of lowercase ASCII letters (`a`–`z`) or digits (`0`–`9`), `MUST` be at least one character long, `SHOULD` start with a letter and not exceed 20 characters, and `MUST NOT` use the reserved name `data` [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). Third, under **Privacy & Security**, the specification advises that sensitive information `SHOULD NOT` be placed inside context attributes—including `id`, `source`, and `type`—because producers, intermediaries, and consumers `MAY` introspect and log context attributes in plaintext [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md).

Implementers must also distinguish **core `REQUIRED` attributes** from **extension-scoped `REQUIRED` attributes**. Documented CloudEvents extensions frequently mark their own attributes as `REQUIRED`—for example, `traceparent` in Distributed Tracing (`cloudevents/extensions/distributed-tracing.md`), `sequence` in Sequence (`cloudevents/extensions/sequence.md`), `severitynumber` in Severity (`cloudevents/extensions/severity.md`), and `opcuastatus` when status is not Good in OPC UA (`cloudevents/extensions/opcua.md`) [spec/cloudevents/extensions/opcua.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/extensions/opcua.md). Every such extension carries an explicit Notational Conventions caveat stating that `REQUIRED` applies only when that extension is used and never expands the universal four-attribute core [spec/cloudevents/extensions/severity.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/extensions/severity.md).

## Wire Representations Across Formats and Protocol Bindings

Because `cloudevents/spec.md` defines an abstract, transport-agnostic data model [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md), official Event Formats and Protocol Bindings project `id`, `source`, `specversion`, and `type` onto distinct wire representations. The matrix below compares how five major specifications map the required attribute set.

| Specification & Status | Wire Container | Mapping of `id`, `source`, `specversion`, `type` | Key Normative Wire Rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **JSON Event Format** (`json-format.md`, v1.0.2) [CloudEvents Specification - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec) | Top-level JSON object [spec/cloudevents/formats/json-format.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/formats/json-format.md) | Top-level JSON strings: `"id"`, `"source"`, `"specversion"`, `"type"` [spec/cloudevents/formats/json-format.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/formats/json-format.md) | Enforced via JSON Schema `"required"` array; JSON `null` `MUST` be decoded as unset/omitted [spec/cloudevents/formats/cloudevents.json at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/formats/cloudevents.json). |
| **HTTP Binary Content Mode** (`http-protocol-binding.md` §3.1, v1.0.2) [CloudEvents Specification - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec) | HTTP 1.1 headers (case-insensitive) [spec/cloudevents/bindings/http-protocol-binding.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/bindings/http-protocol-binding.md) | `ce-id`, `ce-source`, `ce-specversion`, `ce-type` [spec/cloudevents/formats/json-format.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/formats/json-format.md) | Unquoted canonical strings; §3.1.3.2 requires UTF-8 percent-encoding for spaces, quotes, `%`, and non-ASCII [spec/cloudevents/bindings/http-protocol-binding.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/bindings/http-protocol-binding.md). |
| **HTTP Structured Content Mode** (`http-protocol-binding.md` §3.2, v1.0.2) [CloudEvents Specification - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec) | HTTP message body (e.g., `application/cloudevents+json`) [spec/cloudevents/bindings/http-protocol-binding.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/bindings/http-protocol-binding.md) | Encoded per chosen event format inside HTTP body [spec/cloudevents/bindings/http-protocol-binding.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/bindings/http-protocol-binding.md) | Attributes `MUST` appear in the body even if mirrored in `ce-*` headers [spec/cloudevents/bindings/http-protocol-binding.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/bindings/http-protocol-binding.md). |
| **Protobuf Event Format** (`protobuf-format.md` §2.3, v1.0.2) [CloudEvents Specification - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec) | Top-level Protobuf message fields [protobuf-format.md - cloudevents/spec - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/formats/protobuf-format.md) | Explicit typed Protobuf fields for all four required attributes [protobuf-format.md - cloudevents/spec - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/formats/protobuf-format.md) | Separated from optional and extension attributes, which reside in a typed `attributes` map [protobuf-format.md - cloudevents/spec - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/formats/protobuf-format.md). |
| **AMQP Protocol Binding** (`amqp-protocol-binding.md`, v1.0.2) [CloudEvents Specification - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec) | AMQP `application-properties` (binary) or `application data` (structured) [amqp-protocol-binding.md - cloudevents/spec - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/bindings/amqp-protocol-binding.md) | Transferred as AMQP metadata properties (binary) or JSON/event format payload (structured) [amqp-protocol-binding.md - cloudevents/spec - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/bindings/amqp-protocol-binding.md) | Structured-mode implementations `MUST` support the JSON event format [amqp-protocol-binding.md - cloudevents/spec - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/bindings/amqp-protocol-binding.md). |
| **Avro Compact Event Format** (`avro-compact-format.md`, `1.0.3-wip` draft) [spec/cloudevents/working-drafts/avro-compact-format.md at main](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/working-drafts/avro-compact-format.md) | Fixed Avro 1.9.0 binary record [spec/cloudevents/working-drafts/avro-compact-format.md at main](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/working-drafts/avro-compact-format.md) | Explicit Avro `string` fields for `id`, `source`, `type`; `specversion` is `N/A` (implicit `"1.0"`) [spec/cloudevents/working-drafts/avro-compact-format.md at main](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/working-drafts/avro-compact-format.md) | Working draft only; supports spec version `1.0` exclusively, omitting `specversion` on the wire [spec/cloudevents/working-drafts/avro-compact-format.md at main](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/working-drafts/avro-compact-format.md). |

In the **JSON Event Format** (`cloudevents/formats/json-format.md` v1.0.2), all required attributes MUST be serialized as top-level JSON strings [spec/cloudevents/formats/json-format.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/formats/json-format.md). The accompanying JSON Schema (`cloudevents/formats/cloudevents.json`) declares `"required": ["id", "source", "specversion", "type"]`, enforcing non-empty strings (such as `"minLength": 1` on `iddef` and `sourcedef`) and `"format": "uri-reference"` on `sourcedef` [spec/cloudevents/formats/cloudevents.json at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/formats/cloudevents.json). Because Section 2.2 of `json-format.md` dictates that decoding a JSON `null` value `MUST` be treated identically to an omitted attribute, setting any required attribute to `null` produces an invalid CloudEvent [spec/cloudevents/formats/json-format.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/formats/json-format.md).

In the **HTTP Protocol Binding** (`cloudevents/bindings/http-protocol-binding.md` v1.0.2), wire encoding varies by sender-selected content mode [spec/cloudevents/bindings/http-protocol-binding.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/bindings/http-protocol-binding.md). Under **Binary Content Mode (§3.1)**, each required attribute maps to an individual `ce-`-prefixed HTTP header (`ce-id`, `ce-source`, `ce-specversion`, `ce-type`), carrying the attribute's unquoted canonical string value [spec/cloudevents/formats/json-format.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/formats/json-format.md). Under **Section 3.1.3.2**, senders `MUST` UTF-8 percent-encode (`%xy`) Space (`U+0020`), Double-quote (`U+0022`), Percent (`U+0025`), and any characters outside printable ASCII (`U+0021`–`U+007E`), while receivers `MUST` reject overlong encodings such as `%C0%A0`—a rule also mirrored verbatim in the NATS Protocol Binding [spec/cloudevents/bindings/http-protocol-binding.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/bindings/http-protocol-binding.md). In practice, however, SDK conformance varies: an issue filed against the specification (`cloudevents/spec#1397`) reported that only two of four measured SDKs implemented the §3.1.3.2 percent-encoding rule, and a Go SDK issue (`cloudevents/sdk-go#1331`) similarly flagged missing HTTP binary percent-encoding [HTTP binary mode does not percent-encode or decode header](https://github.com/cloudevents/sdk-go/issues/1331). Under **Structured Content Mode (§3.2)**, the HTTP `Content-Type` identifies an event format such as `application/cloudevents+json; charset=UTF-8`, and all required attributes `MUST` be encoded in the payload body even if also echoed as `ce-*` headers [spec/cloudevents/bindings/http-protocol-binding.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/bindings/http-protocol-binding.md). **Batched Content Mode (§3.3)** sends an array of complete events under a batch media type such as `application/cloudevents-batch+json`, subject to the core uniform-`specversion` rule [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md).

## Version Evolution and Real-World Implementation Pitfalls

Older enterprise event feeds and legacy webhooks—including historical Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, SAP S/4HANA Event Mesh, and Qlik integrations—sometimes emit CloudEvents **v0.1** payloads whose required attribute names differ substantially from v1.0.x [Qlik Cloud Webhooks: Migration to new event formats is coming](https://community.qlik.com/t5/Official-Support-Articles/Qlik-Cloud-Webhooks-Migration-to-new-event-formats-is-coming/ta-p/2528660). The required attribute names stabilized in **v0.2** (December 6, 2018) and have remained unchanged through **v1.0** (October 24, 2019), **v1.0.1** (December 2020), and **v1.0.2** (February 5, 2022) [CloudEvents |](https://cloudevents.io/).

| Specification Version | Release Date | Required Attribute Names | Notable Normative Changes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **v0.1** | April 20, 2018 [spec/docs/ROADMAP.md at main · cloudevents/spec - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/docs/ROADMAP.md) | `cloudEventsVersion`, `eventType`, `source`, `eventID` [administering-oracle-analytics-cloud-oracle-cloud-infrastructure-gen](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/analytics-cloud/acoci/administering-oracle-analytics-cloud-oracle-cloud-infrastructure-gen-2.pdf) | Mixed camelCase naming; `"0.1"` version string; nested `extensions` object [Qlik Cloud Webhooks: Migration to new event formats is coming](https://community.qlik.com/t5/Official-Support-Articles/Qlik-Cloud-Webhooks-Migration-to-new-event-formats-is-coming/ta-p/2528660). |
| **v0.2** | December 6, 2018 [spec/docs/ROADMAP.md at main · cloudevents/spec - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/docs/ROADMAP.md) | `specversion`, `type`, `source`, `id` [cloudevents-spec/spec.md at master - GitHub](https://github.com/alanconway/cloudevents-spec/blob/master/spec.md) | Introduced lowercase ASCII attribute naming (`[a-z0-9]`, ≤20 chars recommended); HTTP binary mode still used JSON-quoted header values [cloudevents-spec/spec.md at master - GitHub](https://github.com/alanconway/cloudevents-spec/blob/master/spec.md). |
| **v1.0 / v1.0.1 / v1.0.2** | Oct 24, 2019 / Dec 2020 / Feb 5, 2022 [CloudEvents /](https://cloudevents.io/) | `id`, `source`, `specversion`, `type` [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md) | Removed "conditional" attributes (leaving only `REQUIRED` and `OPTIONAL`); locked `specversion` to `"1.0"`; formalized `source` + `id` uniqueness, Unicode exclusions, non-empty constraints, and unquoted percent-encoded HTTP binary headers [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). |

Developers implementing or validating CloudEvents in production should guard against three recurring pitfalls:

- **Emitting Patch Numbers in `specversion`:** Some vendor migration notes have erroneously shown `"specversion": "1.0.2"` when migrating from v0.1 to v1.0.2 [Changelog | Qlik Developer Portal](https://qlik.dev/changelog/). Strict validators and SDKs—such as the CloudEvents Python SDK (which checks `specversion == "1.0"`) and Azure's Java `CloudEvent` model (which fixes the field to `"1.0"`)—reject `"1.0.2"` as non-compliant [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md).
- **Confusing SDK Constructor Defaults with Wire Requirements:** Several SDKs, including the CloudEvents Python SDK and the Azure SDK for Java, only require callers to supply `source` and `type` during object construction, automatically generating a UUID for `id` and defaulting `specversion` to `"1.0"` [CloudEvent Class | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/java/api/com.azure.core.models.cloudevent?view=azure-java-stable). Producers constructing raw JSON payloads or HTTP binary headers without an SDK must populate all four attributes explicitly, because compliant receivers validate all four on ingestion [spec/cloudevents/formats/cloudevents.json at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/formats/cloudevents.json).
- **Treating Empty Strings or JSON `null` as Present Attributes:** Both `cloudevents/spec.md` and `cloudevents.json` prohibit empty strings for the required attributes, and `json-format.md` mandates treating JSON `null` as omitted [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md). Serializing `"id": ""` or `"type": null` fails validation even though the property keys exist in the payload [spec/cloudevents/spec.md at main - GitHub](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md).
